article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Nitro Cookies × Blue Sherbert
Breeder: In House Genetics
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: beta-caryophyllene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, sweet berries, creamy sherbet
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Variable
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

True Blue sits at the intersection of two very different flavor traditions in modern cannabis breeding. One side brings fuel, Cookies funk, and dense resinous flower; the other contributes blueberry sweetness, creamy Sherbert character, and the possibility of striking purple coloration. Instead of producing weed that tastes simply like blueberries, the combination creates a darker and more layered profile in which berries can mingle with gas, earth, cookie dough, cream, and spice. In House Genetics developed the cultivar from Nitro Cookies and Blue Sherbert, giving True Blue a genetic background filled with Cookies, OG, Blueberry , Sherbert, and Kush influences.

This particular cultivar should not be confused with True Blueberry, the older DJ Short cannabis line that is sometimes shortened informally to “True Blue.” The In House Genetics strain covered here is specifically documented as Nitro Cookies × Blue Sherbert and was released as feminized seed. Its breeder-listed flowering period is 56–65 days, putting most plants near eight to nine weeks of bloom. For growers interested in modern resin-heavy marijuana with blueberry and Sherbert ancestry, True Blue combines substantial genetic complexity with a relatively practical flowering schedule.
Genetics and Lineage

True Blue begins with Nitro Cookies, a hybrid associated with Gasmask × Animal Cookies . That parent supplies much of the darker personality in the cross. Animal Cookies brings the dense flower structure, sweet dough, earthy Kush character, and potency associated with the Cookies family, while Gasmask contributes a much sharper fuel and chemical edge. The result is a parent capable of adding resin production, pungency, and considerable physical weight to its offspring.

Blue Sherbert provides the other half of the equation. Its documented lineage runs through Blue Cookies × Sunset Sherbert . Blue Cookies itself combines Girl Scout Cookies with Blueberry, while Sunset Sherbert traces through Girl Scout Cookies and Pink Panties . That means Cookies genetics appear repeatedly throughout the True Blue family tree, but the Blueberry component introduces older Purple Thai, Afghani , and Thai ancestry that broadens the aromatic range considerably.

This repeated Cookies influence helps explain why the cultivar should not be viewed as a simple fruit strain. Sweet berry characteristics can be prominent, but they sit within a framework of dense modern hybrid genetics containing Kush, fuel, dessert, and earthy elements. Individual phenotypes may emphasize the blueberry side while others lean toward Nitro Cookies, creating plants with more gas, spice, or dark earthy pungency.
Effects and Experience

True Blue generally fits the profile of a contemporary hybrid rather than an extremely cerebral sativa or heavily narcotic indica. The initial phase can bring a noticeable change in mood, with mental tension becoming less prominent and ordinary activities taking on a more enjoyable quality. Conversation, music, movies, gaming, and relaxed social environments can all suit the early portion of the experience. There may be a creative edge, particularly at moderate amounts, but the mental stimulation is usually accompanied by a gradually developing sense of physical ease.

As the session continues, the heavier genetics become increasingly apparent. Nitro Cookies, Animal Cookies, OG-related ancestry, and the Sherbert family can all contribute to an experience that settles into the body rather than remaining entirely cerebral. Shoulders may relax, movement feels less urgent, and the initial mental brightness can develop into a calmer, more introspective state. Larger servings are more likely to push the strain toward evening territory, especially for consumers with lower THC tolerance.

No authoritative breeder THC range has been published for the original True Blue release. That omission matters because modern cannabis databases frequently attach potency figures to strain names as though every plant were chemically identical. In reality, phenotype selection, lighting, plant health, harvest timing, drying, curing, and laboratory methodology can all alter cannabinoid concentration. A tested batch should therefore take priority over a generic THC number.
Medical Benefits

True Blue has not been studied in controlled medical trials as an individual marijuana cultivar. Its potential medical appeal is instead based on the general effects associated with THC-dominant hybrid cannabis. Consumers seeking an experience that combines mental decompression with physical relaxation may find this type of profile useful when temporarily dealing with stress, low mood, or difficulty shifting out of a mentally demanding day.

As the physical component increases, some medical cannabis consumers may also appreciate the cultivar when seeking temporary relief from everyday muscular tension, minor discomfort, or reduced appetite. Its gradual transition from cerebral lift into heavier relaxation could make later-day use more suitable than periods requiring maximum alertness. Depending on phenotype and dose, the plant may eventually become considerably more sedating than its opening effects suggest.

Potent marijuana can also produce unwanted responses, including dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, elevated heart rate, and impaired coordination. People using cannabis for a diagnosed health condition should consider the cannabinoid and terpene analysis of the actual flower and consult an appropriate medical professional rather than assuming the True Blue name predicts a specific therapeutic outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Blueberry and dark fruit provide the most obvious connection to the cultivar’s name, but True Blue has substantially more aromatic depth beneath them. Blue Sherbert can contribute ripe berries, sweet cream, sugary fruit, and dessert-like notes, while Nitro Cookies pushes the profile toward fuel, earth, dough, pepper, and occasional chemical sharpness. The strongest phenotypes may smell almost like blueberry pastry layered over gasoline and earthy cannabis.

Breaking apart the flowers often changes the balance. Sweetness becomes more concentrated at first, followed by a pungent wave of spice and gas from inside the bud. On inhalation, blueberry and creamy Sherbert qualities can dominate, while the exhale becomes darker and more savory, carrying earth, cookie dough, pepper, and fuel. Some plants may express more citrus or floral sweetness depending on which side of the family tree is dominant.

There is no official terpene laboratory profile that can be assigned universally to the cultivar. Beta-caryophyllene, limonene, myrcene, and linalool are plausible contributors to the spicy, citrus, earthy, and floral qualities associated with its ancestry, but exact terpene dominance can only be established through testing of an individual harvest.
Growing Information

True Blue is a photoperiod cultivar released in feminized seed form. The documented flowering period runs from approximately 56 to 65 days, giving growers an eight-to-nine-week window for most plants. That schedule is convenient for indoor production because it allows the flowers sufficient time to build density and trichome coverage without stretching into the extended flowering periods associated with traditional tropical cannabis.

Growth characteristics can vary according to phenotype, but the genetic background suggests a branching modern-hybrid structure rather than extreme sativa height. Topping or low-stress training during vegetative growth can help create several evenly illuminated tops. Allowing adequate airflow through the interior canopy is worthwhile because Cookies- and Sherbert-influenced flowers can become dense as maturity approaches. Lower growth receiving little direct light can be selectively removed so the plant concentrates resources on productive flowering sites.

Color expression is one of the cultivar’s potential attractions. The Blueberry and Sherbert ancestry may produce violet, purple, or blue-tinged calyxes in certain phenotypes, particularly as plants reach maturity. Genetics are more important than cold temperatures for establishing this capability, although cooler nighttime conditions can sometimes make anthocyanin pigmentation more visible. Excessively lowering temperatures solely to force color can reduce growth and should not be treated as necessary.

No authoritative breeder yield figure is available, so claims of a specific number of grams per square meter should be treated cautiously. Healthy plants under strong lighting can nevertheless produce substantial resinous flowers when root space, nutrition, airflow, and environmental conditions remain consistent. Outdoors, the roughly nine-week flowering window generally places harvest during autumn, with the exact date determined by latitude and when flowering naturally begins.
FAQ
What are the genetics of True Blue?
The In House Genetics version of True Blue is Nitro Cookies × Blue Sherbert. The breeder’s documented flowering period is 56–65 days, and the cultivar was released as feminized seed.
Is True Blue the same as True Blueberry?

No. True Blueberry is associated with breeder DJ Short and belongs to the famous Blueberry genetic family. The True Blue strain covered here was bred by In House Genetics from Nitro Cookies and Blue Sherbert. Similar naming has caused the two cultivars to be confused in some strain descriptions .
Is True Blue indica or sativa?

It is best described simply as a hybrid. Its genetic background combines Cookies, OG, Sherbert, Blueberry, Kush, and older sativa ancestry, giving it both cerebral and physical characteristics rather than a clearly documented breeder percentage.
What does True Blue taste like?

Blueberry, sweet berries, cream, and Sherbert-like fruit are balanced by gas, cookie dough, earth, and spice. Some phenotypes may lean heavily toward sweet blueberry flavors, while others emphasize the darker Nitro Cookies side.
How long does True Blue take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 56–65 days, or roughly eight to nine weeks. Growers should still examine flower and trichome maturity rather than harvesting solely according to the calendar.
Final Thoughts on True Blue

True Blue is a good example of how modern cannabis breeders can use familiar flavor families without creating a predictable result. Blue Sherbert supplies blueberry, fruit, cream, and potential purple coloration, while Nitro Cookies adds the gas, earth, resin, and heavier character necessary to keep the finished strain from tasting like another straightforward berry hybrid. Beneath those parents is an extensive family tree involving Blueberry, Girl Scout Cookies, Sunset Sherbert, Animal Cookies, OG Kush , and older Thai and Afghani genetics.

For growers, the eight-to-nine-week flowering period and feminized format make the cultivar relatively practical despite its complex ancestry. For consumers, its strongest appeal is contrast: sweet berries against fuel, creamy Sherbert against earthy Cookies, and an upbeat beginning that gradually develops into deeper physical relaxation. True Blue may share its name with other marijuana varieties, but the In House Genetics Nitro Cookies × Blue Sherbert version has a genetic identity entirely its own.
